newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: UN observers move to camps for rebel disarmament.
newsitem.headline: UN observers move to camps for rebel disarmament.

text.p: Dozens of U.N. military observers moved on Friday to camps in Guatemala where they were to oversee the disarmament of guerrillas laying down their arms after 36 years of civil war.
The 155 so-called "blue berets" will oversee disarmament at eight camps in six rural areas.

Before March 3, when several thousand ex-guerrillas will move into the camps, the U.N. mission will prepare equipment for registering each guerrilla, giving official registration cards, and administering medical checks.

More than three decades of civil war ended in this Central American nation on Dec. 29 when the government and leftist rebels of the Guatemalan National Revolutionary Unit (URNG) signed a historic peace treaty.
Rebel disarmament is one aspect of the peace agreement.

"Among the URNG here there are certainly people who have been fighting in very difficult terrain for 10-15 or even more years so they will need counselling to get back into civil society," David Stephen, director of the United Nations Mission for the Verification of Human Rights in Guatemala, told Reuters on Friday.
Stephen said the ex-guerrillas must leave the camps, which are mostly constructed on land rented from farmers and ranchers, by May 3.

The entire demobilization operation, including the $2.5 million U.N. observation mission, will cost an estimated $15 million. International donors funded provisional housing, electricity and drinking water for the camps, and in some cases construction of access roads to the camps.

The United Nations moderated Guatemalan peace talks, but the "blue beret" mission was held up for two weeks in January when China briefly used its veto power in the U.N. Security Council to block a resolution to send the observers.
